s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive skin lesions with systemic involvement
salient_findings: Purpura and ecchymoses with progression over 1 year
Abnormal liver function test results and renal impairment
key_facts: 1-year history of purpura, ecchymoses, anorexia, and weight loss
Medical history of alcohol abuse and cognitive impairment
Purpura and ecchymoses initially periorbital, progressed over 12 months
Elder abuse excluded
Waxy yellow papules and plaques with purpura in multiple body regions
Anemia, abnormal liver function test results, and renal impairment with moderate proteinuria
Normal serum protein electrophoresis (SPEP) and immunofixation urine protein electrophoresis test results
Unremarkable radiological studies
Punch biopsy showed upper dermal amorphous eosinophilic deposits
Congo red staining results were positive
Polarizing light microscopy demonstrated pale apple-green birefringence

shortlist.label: Primary systemic amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of purpura, ecchymoses, and systemic involvement, along with positive Congo red staining and apple-green birefringence on biopsy

shortlist.label: Senile systemic amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's age and clinical presentation of waxy yellow papules and plaques with purpura, consistent with senile amyloidosis

shortlist.label: Lipoid proteinosis
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical presentation of waxy yellow papules and plaques, although less likely given the biopsy findings

shortlist.label: Secondary systemic amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Possible association with chronic inflammation or infection, although less likely given the clinical presentation and biopsy findings

shortlist.label: Amyloidosis associated with multiple myeloma
shortlist.why_kept: Although the serum protein electrophoresis (SPEP) and immunofixation urine protein electrophoresis test results were normal, this diagnosis cannot be entirely excluded without further evaluation

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with purpura, ecchymoses, anorexia, weight loss, and the biopsy findings of upper dermal amorphous eosinophilic deposits with positive Congo red staining and apple-green birefringence under polarized light microscopy are characteristic of amyloidosis. The absence of multiple myeloma (normal SPEP and immunofixation) and the lack of a clear chronic inflammatory condition point towards primary systemic amyloidosis.

rejected.label: Senile systemic amyloidosis
rejected.why: Typically presents with cardiac involvement and less commonly with skin manifestations, which are prominent in this case

rejected.label: Lipoid proteinosis
rejected.why: Characterized by hoarseness, which is not mentioned, and the biopsy findings do not match

rejected.label: Secondary systemic amyloidosis
rejected.why: Usually associated with chronic inflammatory diseases, which are not mentioned in the case

rejected.label: Amyloidosis associated with multiple myeloma
rejected.why: Normal SPEP and immunofixation results make this diagnosis unlikely
